lines: Imagine falling from the sky through a violent storm and waking up alone in a deadly jungle.
On 24 December 1971 a passenger plane is struck by lightning and breaks apart midair.
Seventeen year old Juliane Koepcke falls about 3000 meters while still strapped to her seat row.
She wakes up on the dark forest floor with a broken collarbone and a deep arm cut.
She also suffers from a painful eye injury and a severe concussion after the terrifying plunge.
Her biologist father previously taught her that following flowing water always leads back to people.
She finds a tiny creek and begins walking through the dense and dangerous Peruvian rainforest.
Days pass slowly as she follows the winding water toward a larger and safer river.
Up to 14 other passengers survive the initial crash but tragically die before any rescue arrives.
She spends 11 long days completely alone in the unforgiving jungle facing unimaginable odds.
After 9 days of difficult travel she finally discovers a remote lumberjack camp by the river.
She is found by local workers who provide medical help and bring her back to safety.
Juliane remains the only official survivor of LANSA Flight 508 against all odds and expectations.
Would you have the mental strength to survive 11 days alone in the dangerous rainforest?

lines: If the city grid fails completely, do not light a single candle inside your room.
Mark stands inside a tall office building as grid power drops without any warning.
The total dark hits fast, giving Mark exactly 48 hours to survive this blackout.
Panic spreads outside on dark streets, but Mark stays focused and walks to shelter now.
He moves fast and decides to enter shelter before pitch darkness covers everything.
One. Mark stores water early by filling all containers and the bathtub right now.
Filling containers and the bathtub while taps work secures his life water.
Two. Mark uses flashlights only because candles cause terrible fires during blackouts.
Bright battery light protects his shelter without creating open fire hazards tonight.
Three. Mark keeps the fridge closed tight so food stays safe for 4 hours.
A full freezer left closed keeps food safe for about 48 hours.
He never runs a generator, grill, or camp stove indoors because carbon monoxide kills silently.
Safe inside the tall office building, Mark prepares for the dark night.
He followed every safety rule and locked down his blackout shelter securely.
It was the perfect plan, but Mark faces one dangerous problem in the dark building.
Someone lit a camp stove downstairs, filling the enclosed building with silent carbon monoxide.
part1.cliffhanger: Someone downstairs lit a camp stove indoors, filling the locked-down building with lethal, unseen carbon monoxide.
